statement.p: A ball is dropped from a state of rest at time t=0.
The distance traveled after t seconds is s(t)=16t^2 ft.
(a) How far does the ball travel during the time interval [9,{9.5}] ?
(c) Compute the average velocity over time intervals [9, 9.01] , [9, 9.001] , [9, 9.0001] , [8.9999, 9] , [8.999, 9] , [8.99, 9] .
Use this to estimate the object's instantaneous velocity at t={9} .

static.solution:
Solution:
(a) Galileo's formula is s(t)=16t^2. The ball thus travels
\Delta s=s(9.5)-s(9)=16 \cdot 9.5^2 - 16 \cdot 9^2 = 148 \enspace ft.
(b) The average velocity over [9, 9.5] is
\frac {\Delta s} {\Delta t} = \frac {s(9.5)-s(9)} {9.5 - 9} = \frac {16 \cdot 9.5^2 - 16 \cdot 9^2} {9.5 - 9} =\frac {148}{0.5} = 296 \enspace ft/s.
(c)
time interval average velocity
[9, 9.01] 288.159999999993
[9, 9.001] 288.015999999743
[9, 9.0001] 288.001599999461
[8.9999, 9] 287.998399999196
[8.999, 9] 287.983999999824
[8.99, 9] 287.839999999983
The instantaneous velocity at t=9 is 288 ft/s.
